snippet.title: Macaulay Culkin's Heartbreaking Tribute to Catherine O'Hara #macaulayculkin #viral #shorts
snippet.description:
At the 78th Emmy Awards on September 14, 2026, Macaulay Culkin delivered an emotional tribute to Catherine O'Hara, who died in January at age 71 . Culkin joined O'Hara's Schitt's Creek co-stars Annie Murphy and Dan Levy on stage to honor the actress who played his mother in the Home Alone films.

"She Was My Mom"
To Culkin, O'Hara was more than a co-star. "She wasn't just a wife to Bo and mother to Matthew and Luke," he said. "She was my mom. She was our mama, and by extension, she's all of our mama" . He urged viewers to call their mothers, reflecting on how O'Hara continued to show up for him decades after they starred together.

The Home Alone Joke That Hit Different
Referencing the premise of the two Home Alone films—where O'Hara's Kate McCallister famously forgets her son Kevin twice—Culkin closed with a line that brought the room to tears: "She may have forgotten me twice, but we will always remember her" .

A Mother to Everyone
Culkin said O'Hara "always showed up when I asked her to, because that was Catherine. That's what she did. She showed up" . The tribute opened the Emmys' In Memoriam segment, honoring an actress who was a mother to her on-screen kids across two iconic shows.

snippet.description:
This is a story of tribute, nostalgia, and a beautiful moment of remembrance at the Emmy Awards. Macaulay Culkin honored the late Catherine O'Hara with words that touched the hearts of millions: "She may have forgotten me… twice, but we will always remember her."

Let's break down this emotional moment. Macaulay Culkin and Catherine O'Hara shared a screen history that is beloved by millions. They starred together in Home Alone and Home Alone 2: Lost in New York. She played Kate McCallister, the mother who famously forgot her son Kevin at home—twice. He played Kevin McCallister, the child who was left behind, who defended his home, and who ultimately taught us all about family, forgiveness, and Christmas.

Their on-screen relationship was funny, chaotic, and deeply heartfelt. And off-screen, their bond was real. Catherine O'Hara was a comedy legend. She was a genius. She was a kind soul. And her passing left a hole in the hearts of everyone who loved her.

Macaulay Culkin took the stage at the Emmys. He was there to honor her. He was there to remember her. He was there to say goodbye. And he did it with grace, with humor, and with love. He referenced the iconic joke—that she forgot him twice. It was a nod to the films that made them both legends. But then he said something more powerful: "We will always remember her."

The photo captures the tribute. In the top image, Macaulay Culkin is standing on the Emmy stage. He is wearing a white suit. He is looking at the audience. He is paying tribute. Beside him are other presenters. They are there to honor the fallen legends. In the bottom image, we see a scene from Home Alone 2. Catherine O'Hara is looking shocked. Macaulay Culkin is looking at her. It is a moment from the film. It is a memory. It is a legacy.

The reaction on social media has been overwhelming. "This is beautiful. She was a legend," one user wrote. Another added, "Macaulay's tribute was perfect." A third commented, "I am crying. This is the most beautiful thing I have seen today."

His story is a reminder that great actors never die. They live on in their work. They live on in our memories. They live on in the hearts of the people they touched. Catherine O'Hara was a legend. She was a mother on screen. She was a friend off screen. She was a genius. She was a gift.

She may have forgotten Kevin McCallister twice. But she never forgot how to make us laugh. She never forgot how to make us cry. She never forgot how to make us feel. And we will never forget her.

RIP to a true legend. Catherine O'Hara, you will always be remembered.
